en: be on brotherly terms; be on fraternal terms

examples.ko: 저와 김 사장님은 십 년 넘게 호형호제하며 지내요.
examples.en: Mr. Kim and I have been like brothers for over ten years.
We met in the army and have been like brothers ever since.
My father and the neighbor are on brotherly terms.
He was the one who first suggested we treat each other like brothers.

examples.ko: 호형호제하던 친구와 싸워서 마음이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: I feel bad because I had a fight with a friend who was like a brother to me.

examples.ko: 호형호제할 정도로 친한 사람이 몇 명 있어요?
examples.en: How many people are you close enough with to call each other brothers?

explain: 보통 '~와/과 호형호제하다'처럼 '와/과'와 함께 써요. 대화에서는 '형 동생 하다'라고 풀어서 말하는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: It is usually used with '와/과', as in '~와/과 호형호제하다'. In conversation people also say it more plainly as '형 동생 하다'.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 호혜적 관계를 오래 이어 왔어요.
examples.en: The two countries have kept up a mutually beneficial relationship for a long time.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 호혜적 원칙에 따라 협력해요.
examples.en: Our company cooperates on the principle of reciprocity.

examples.ko: 호혜적 거래가 되려면 양쪽 모두 이익이 있어야 해요.
examples.en: For a deal to be reciprocal, both sides need to benefit.

examples.ko: 두 학교가 호혜적 교류를 시작하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two schools decided to start a reciprocal exchange.

examples.ko: 이번 합의는 호혜적 성격이 강하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this agreement is strongly reciprocal in nature.
A reciprocal attitude of helping each other is important.

explain: '호혜적 관계', '호혜적 협력'처럼 뒤에 명사를 바로 붙여 써요. 주로 나라나 기업 사이의 일을 말하는 뉴스와 글에서 많이 나와요. '호혜적인'이나 '호혜적이다' 꼴로도 써요.
explain_en: It goes directly before a noun, as in '호혜적 관계' or '호혜적 협력'. It appears mostly in news and writing about relations between countries or companies. You can also say '호혜적인' or '호혜적이다'.

examples.en: Grandmother has become white-haired before I knew it.

examples.ko: 공원에서 호호백발의 할아버지가 책을 읽고 계세요.
examples.en: A white-haired old man is reading a book in the park.

examples.ko: 우리 둘이 호호백발이 될 때까지 함께해요.
examples.en: Let's stay together until we are both old and gray.
I helped a white-haired elderly person cross the road.
My mother, whom I hadn't seen in a long time, had gone completely white-haired.

examples.ko: 저도 호호백발 할머니가 되면 여행을 많이 다닐 거예요.
examples.en: When I become a white-haired grandmother, I'll travel a lot.

explain: 보통 '호호백발 할머니', '호호백발 할아버지'처럼 나이 든 사람 앞에 붙여 써요. '호호백발이 될 때까지'는 오래도록 함께 산다는 뜻으로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It usually comes before an elderly person, as in '호호백발 할머니' or '호호백발 할아버지'. '호호백발이 될 때까지' is a common way to say 'for a very long time together'.

en: being luxurious; being sumptuous; being lavish

examples.ko: 이런 호화판 생활을 하다 보면 본분을 잊게 돼요.
examples.en: If you live a lavish life like this, you end up forgetting your duty.
A celebrity's lavish wedding was in the news.
There's a rumor that they went on a luxurious trip abroad.

examples.ko: 그 회사 임원들은 호화판 파티를 열었어요.
examples.en: The company's executives threw a lavish party.
They were criticized for building a luxurious government building with taxes.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 호화판 잔치를 할 형편이 아니에요.
examples.en: My family can't afford a lavish feast.

explain: '호화판 생활', '호화판 결혼식'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 쓰고, 지나치다고 비판하는 느낌이 있어요. 단순히 화려하다고 말할 때는 '호화롭다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used before a noun, as in '호화판 생활' or '호화판 결혼식', and often carries a critical sense of excess. For simply describing something as luxurious, use '호화롭다'.

examples.ko: 올여름은 혹서가 이어져 온열 질환자가 늘었어요.
examples.en: The extreme heat continued this summer, and heat-related illnesses increased.

examples.ko: 혹서 속에서도 일을 해야 하는 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: There are people who have to work even in the extreme heat.
They made equipment that withstands extreme heat and cold.
During the hottest season, cut back on outdoor activities in the daytime.
Electricity use rose sharply because of the extreme heat.
The soldiers safely finished their extreme-heat training.

explain: 반대말은 '혹한'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '무더위'나 '폭염'이라고 하고, '혹서'는 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 나와요. 가장 더운 시기를 '혹서기'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '혹한' (severe cold). In daily talk people say '무더위' or '폭염', while '혹서' appears more in news and writing. The hottest period is called '혹서기'.

examples.en: Some people call this film a masterpiece.

examples.ko: 혹자는 아침형 인간이 더 성공한다고 주장해요.
examples.en: Some claim that morning people are more successful.
As some say, it isn't an easy thing.

examples.ko: 혹자는 그를 천재라고 부르지만 저는 노력가라고 생각해요.
examples.en: Some call him a genius, but I think he is a hard worker.

examples.ko: 혹자에게는 이 방법이 맞지 않을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: This method may not suit some people.

examples.ko: 혹자가 그렇게 말했다고 해서 다 맞는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because someone said so doesn't mean it's all correct.

explain: '어떤 사람'을 조금 격식 있게 말하는 표현이라서 글이나 발표에서 '혹자는 ~라고 말한다'처럼 많이 써요. 한 사람일 수도 있고 여러 사람일 수도 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '어떤 사람들은'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a somewhat formal way to say 'a certain person', often seen in writing and presentations as '혹자는 ~라고 말한다'. It can mean one person or several. In daily conversation people say '어떤 사람들은'.

examples.en: Their daughter has reached marriageable age, so her parents are worried.
These days the age for marrying has become much later.

examples.ko: 혼기를 놓쳤다는 말을 요즘은 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: People don't say 'you missed your marriageable age' much these days.

examples.ko: 혼기에 접어든 아들에게 소개가 많이 들어와요.
examples.en: Many introductions come in for their son, who has reached marriageable age.
A gathering was held for single men and women of marriageable age.

examples.ko: 그분은 혼기를 훌쩍 넘겼지만 아주 행복해 보여요.
examples.en: She is well past the so-called marriageable age, but she looks very happy.

explain: '혼기가 차다', '혼기를 놓치다'처럼 자주 써요. '결혼 적령기'와 비슷한데, 나이로 결혼 시기를 말하는 것이라서 요즘은 듣기 불편해하는 사람도 있으니 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: It is often used as '혼기가 차다' or '혼기를 놓치다'. It is close to '결혼 적령기', but because it ties marriage to age, some people find it uncomfortable to hear, so use it with care.

en: proposal of marriage; offer of marriage

examples.ko: 이모 덕분에 좋은 집안과 혼담이 오갔어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my aunt, marriage talks started with a good family.
I heard she suffered for a while after the marriage talks fell through.
My mother turned down the marriage proposal her friend brought.

examples.ko: 혼담이 들어왔지만 아직 결혼할 생각은 없어요.
examples.en: A marriage offer came in, but I have no plans to marry yet.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손녀의 혼담을 직접 챙기셨다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the grandmother took care of her granddaughter's marriage talks herself.

examples.ko: 혼담이 잘 풀려서 내년 봄에 결혼식을 한대요.
examples.en: The marriage talks went well, so they're having the wedding next spring.

explain: 집안이나 소개해 주는 사람을 통해 결혼 이야기가 오가는 것을 말해서 옛날 느낌이 있어요. '혼담이 오가다', '혼담이 들어오다', '혼담이 깨지다'로 자주 써요. 요즘 일상에서는 '결혼 얘기'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to marriage talks arranged through families or matchmakers, so it has an old-fashioned feel. Common patterns are '혼담이 오가다', '혼담이 들어오다' and '혼담이 깨지다'. In everyday speech people often say '결혼 얘기' instead.

en: period of confusion; time of chaos

examples.ko: 전쟁 직후 혼란기에 많은 사람이 고향을 떠났어요.
examples.en: Many people left their hometowns during the chaotic period right after the war.
Adolescence is also called a time of confusion for the mind.
The more chaotic the times, the more calmly you must judge.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 오랜 혼란기를 지나 안정을 되찾았어요.
examples.en: That country passed through a long period of turmoil and regained stability.

examples.ko: 새 제도가 시작되는 혼란기에는 실수가 많아요.
examples.en: In the confused period when a new system starts, there are many mistakes.

examples.ko: 우리 회사도 지금 혼란기를 겪고 있어요.
examples.en: Our company is also going through a period of confusion right now.

explain: 사회나 역사뿐 아니라 회사나 개인의 어수선한 시기에도 써요. '과도기'는 한 상태에서 다른 상태로 바뀌어 가는 중간 시기이고, '혼란기'는 질서가 없어 어지러운 시기라는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It can describe a messy period not only in society or history but also for a company or a person. '과도기' is the in-between period while changing from one state to another, whereas '혼란기' stresses disorder and confusion.

en: be scared to death; be frightened out of one's wits

examples.ko: 갑자기 큰 소리가 나서 모두 혼비백산했어요.
examples.en: A loud noise suddenly came and everyone was scared out of their wits.
When the earthquake hit, people panicked and ran outside.
The child cried in terror at the sound of thunder.
I was scared half to death when I suddenly saw a snake on the road.

examples.ko: 불이 났다는 말에 혼비백산한 직원들이 밖으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The employees, panicked by the news of a fire, came outside.

examples.ko: 혼비백산할 정도로 놀라서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: I was so shocked I was frightened out of my wits and couldn't speak.

explain: 몹시 놀라서 정신이 없을 때 쓰는 센 표현이에요. 일상에서 가볍게 놀랐을 때는 '깜짝 놀라다'라고 하고, '기겁하다'도 비슷하게 써요. 이야기하면서 조금 과장해서 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a strong expression for being so shocked that you lose your composure. For mild surprise people say '깜짝 놀라다', and '기겁하다' is similar. It often appears when telling a story with a bit of exaggeration.

examples.en: My older cousin is getting married next year.
I was busy over the weekend because I went to a relative's wedding.
With the wedding approaching, both sets of parents met.

examples.ko: 이모는 혼사 준비로 요즘 정신이 없으세요.
examples.en: My aunt has been swamped lately preparing for the wedding.

examples.ko: 혼사는 두 사람만이 아니라 집안의 일이라고 해요.
examples.en: They say a marriage is a matter for the families, not just the two people.
The date of the wedding has been set for next month.

explain: 결혼식만이 아니라 결혼에 얽힌 준비와 이야기 전체를 말해서 집안일이라는 느낌이 있어요. '혼사를 치르다', '혼사를 앞두다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '결혼'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It covers not just the ceremony but the whole business of a marriage, with a sense of being a family matter. It is used in phrases like '혼사를 치르다' and '혼사를 앞두다'. In everyday talk people often just say '결혼'.

en: unison; working as one; being one

examples.en: The players were united as one, so they created the victory.

examples.ko: 온 가족이 혼연일체의 모습으로 이사를 도왔어요.
examples.en: The whole family helped with the move as one united team.

examples.ko: 팀이 혼연일체가 되려면 서로 믿어야 해요.
examples.en: For a team to become one, its members have to trust each other.
The employees overcame the crisis as one.
It was a show where the singing and dancing blended into one.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 혼연일체가 되어 불을 껐어요.
examples.en: The villagers united as one and put out the fire.

explain: 여럿이 한마음으로 하나가 된 모습을 말하고, '혼연일체가 되다', '혼연일체를 이루다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '한마음 한뜻'은 더 쉬운 말이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 노래와 춤처럼 서로 잘 어우러지는 것에도 써요.
explain_en: It describes many people becoming one in spirit, used as '혼연일체가 되다' or '혼연일체를 이루다'. '한마음 한뜻' is an easier, similar expression. It also applies to things that blend well, like song and dance.

examples.en: She was so shocked that she fainted on the spot.

examples.ko: 더위 속에 서 있던 학생이 혼절했어요.
examples.en: A student who had been standing in the heat passed out.
My mother nearly fainted when she heard the news.
They took the person who had fainted straight to the hospital.
In the drama, the main character collapses from grief.

examples.ko: 피를 보면 혼절할 것 같아서 무서워요.
examples.en: I'm afraid because I feel I'd faint if I saw blood.

explain: '기절하다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 글이나 드라마 같은 말투예요. 일상 대화에서는 '기절하다'나 '쓰러지다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 큰 충격이나 슬픔으로 정신을 잃는 장면에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used like '기절하다' but sounds more literary or dramatic. In daily conversation '기절하다' or '쓰러지다' is much more natural. It suits scenes where someone loses consciousness from great shock or grief.

en: a severe scolding; a good telling-off

examples.en: I lied and got a real scolding from my mom.
I came home late and got a good scolding from my father.
The teacher gave the playing kids a stern scolding.

examples.ko: 다음에 또 그러면 혼쭐을 내 줄 거예요.
examples.en: If you do that again next time, I'll give you a real talking-to.

examples.ko: 시험을 망쳐서 혼쭐이 날까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I failed my exam and I'm worried I'll be scolded hard.

examples.ko: 그 가게 주인한테 혼쭐난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once got a stern scolding from that shop's owner.

explain: 거의 '혼쭐나다', '혼쭐내다'로만 써요. '혼나다'와 비슷하지만 단단히 크게 야단맞는 느낌이 더 강해요. '혼쭐을 내 주다'는 따끔하게 가르쳐 준다는 느낌으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used almost only as '혼쭐나다' or '혼쭐내다'. It is like '혼나다' but with a stronger sense of being scolded thoroughly. '혼쭐을 내 주다' can also mean teaching someone a sharp lesson.

examples.en: It rained, so the river water is muddy.
The air was so stuffy that I opened the window.
It is hard for fish to live in murky water.
The mood of the election must not become corrupted.
When my mind feels clouded, I take a walk.
Many people feel that politics is murky and unclean.

explain: 물이나 공기가 흐릴 때뿐 아니라 정치, 사회, 분위기가 어지럽고 깨끗하지 않을 때도 써요. 반대말은 '맑다'나 '깨끗하다'예요. 일상에서 물이나 공기를 말할 때는 '탁하다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: It describes not only cloudy water or air but also politics, society or atmosphere that is messy and not clean. Its opposites are '맑다' and '깨끗하다'. For water or air in daily talk, '탁하다' is easier.

examples.en: I learned that you must not treat guests poorly.
That shop doesn't treat even regular customers badly.

examples.ko: 친구가 저를 홀대하는 것 같아서 서운했어요.
examples.en: I felt hurt because it seemed my friend was treating me coldly.

examples.ko: 아무리 바빠도 가족을 홀대해서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: No matter how busy you are, you shouldn't neglect your family.
A review was posted saying they were treated poorly for being foreign.
The incident of treating an elderly person poorly became known, and they apologized.

explain: 반대말은 '환대하다'예요. 비슷한 말로 '푸대접하다'가 있어요. '홀대를 받다'처럼 당하는 쪽에서 말할 때도 많아요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '환대하다' (to welcome warmly). A similar word is '푸대접하다'. You also often hear it from the receiving side, as in '홀대를 받다'.

examples.ko: 아이가 과자를 홀랑 다 먹어 버렸어요.
examples.en: The child ate up all the snacks in no time.
The wind blew my hat clean off.

examples.ko: 월급을 일주일 만에 홀랑 써 버렸어요.
examples.en: I blew my whole paycheck in a week.

examples.ko: 눈 깜짝할 사이에 간식이 홀랑 없어졌어요.
examples.en: The snacks vanished in the blink of an eye.

examples.ko: 바람이 세게 불어서 우산이 홀랑 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: The wind blew hard and my umbrella flipped inside out.
I totally forgot my homework and just played.

explain: 주로 '홀랑 먹어 버리다', '홀랑 써 버리다'처럼 '-아/어 버리다'와 함께 써서 아쉽거나 허무한 느낌을 줘요. 가볍고 편한 말투라서 대화에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is mostly paired with '-아/어 버리다', as in '홀랑 먹어 버리다' or '홀랑 써 버리다', giving a feeling of regret or emptiness. It has a light, casual tone and shows up mostly in conversation.

examples.en: Dandelion seeds flew away in the wind.
Ferns reproduce with spores instead of flowers.
Mold spores float around in the air.
The children blew the dandelion fluff into the air.

examples.ko: 버섯의 홀씨는 아주 작아서 눈에 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: Mushroom spores are so tiny they are hard to see.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 홀씨 식물에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned about spore plants in science class.

explain: '포자'와 같은 뜻의 순우리말이에요. 과학에서는 '포자'를 더 많이 쓰지만 '민들레 홀씨'는 일상에서도 자연스럽게 말해요.
explain_en: It is the native Korean word for '포자' (spore). Science uses '포자' more, but '민들레 홀씨' (dandelion fluff) is natural in everyday speech.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 말 없이 홀연히 떠났어요.
examples.en: He left suddenly without a word.
All of a sudden the fog lifted and the mountain came into view.

examples.ko: 어느 날 홀연히 나타난 낯선 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a stranger who appeared out of nowhere one day.

examples.ko: 친구는 회사를 그만두고 홀연히 여행을 갔어요.
examples.en: My friend quit the company and suddenly went off traveling.

examples.ko: 홀연히 옛 생각이 나서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: Old memories suddenly came back to me and I teared up.
The magician vanished from the stage in an instant.

explain: 이야기나 글 같은 느낌이 있어서 '사라지다', '나타나다', '떠나다'와 자주 함께 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '갑자기'나 '불쑥'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It has a storytelling or literary feel and often appears with '사라지다', '나타나다' and '떠나다'. In daily conversation '갑자기' or '불쑥' sounds more natural.
